rejected.title: What an entrepreneur is
card: An entrepreneur is a person who starts a new business or grows an existing one. They do three main things.
Spots an opportunity
they notice a need or a gap that people would pay to have filled, such as a product that is missing in their town.
Takes a risk
they put in their own money, time or effort, and the business may not work. They could lose what they put in.
Organises resources
they bring together the things a business needs, such as money, equipment, materials and workers, and put them to use.
rejected.remember: An entrepreneur sees an opportunity, takes a risk and brings resources together.

a.q: Ben could do one of these things. Which one makes him an entrepreneur?
opts: Borrowing money to buy a van and start selling toasties
Working set hours at a toastie shop for a weekly wage
Buying a toastie for lunch each day from the same shop
Reading a menu and deciding which toastie to order
a.why: Ben sees a chance to sell food, risks borrowed money and gathers a van and ingredients to start a business. Working for a wage is useful work, but the shop owner carries the risk, not Ben.
a.clue: Who starts a business and could lose money?

b.q: Priya notices that no shop in her Tasmanian town sells fresh bread. She spends her savings on an oven and flour, hires a helper and opens a bakery. Which part of her story shows her taking a risk?
opts: She spends her savings, which she could lose
She notices that the town has no fresh bread
She hires a helper to work in the bakery
She buys an oven and flour for baking
b.why: Spending her own savings means she could lose that money if the bakery fails. Noticing the gap is spotting an opportunity. Buying the oven and flour and hiring a helper is organising resources, though paying for them is where the risk sits.
b.clue: Which step could leave her worse off if the business fails?

version.title: What an entrepreneur is
card: An entrepreneur is a person who starts a new business, or grows one, in the hope of making a profit.
Spots an opportunity
notices a need or want that people would pay to have met, such as no café near a busy beach.
Takes a risk
puts in money, time or effort without knowing if the business will work. If it fails, they can lose what they put in.
Organises resources
brings together what the business needs, such as equipment, materials and workers, and puts them to use.
version.remember: An entrepreneur sees a chance, risks something to chase it, and gathers what the business needs.

a.q: Which person is acting as an entrepreneur?
opts: Ana uses her savings to open a dog-washing van
Ana earns a wage washing dogs at a pet shop
Ana pays a business to wash her dog each month
Ana writes a review of a dog-washing van
a.why: Ana risks her own savings to start a business, so she is acting as an entrepreneur. Working for a wage is tempting, but the pet shop's owner carries the risk, not Ana.
a.clue: Who could lose money if the business fails?

b.q: Hamid notices that cyclists in his town drive an hour to get their bikes fixed. He asks friends if they would pay for repairs closer to home. He has spent nothing yet. Which part of being an entrepreneur is this?
opts: Spotting an opportunity
Taking a financial risk
Organising his resources
Making a profit from sales
b.why: Hamid has found a need that people would pay to have met, which is spotting an opportunity. He has not put in any money yet, so he is not taking a risk.
b.clue: He has noticed something, but he has not spent anything.
